modules.title: Hibernatable WebSockets and Alarms

expected.rationale: Directly addresses every technical objective requested by the intermediate engineer: V8 isolate mechanics, CPU vs I/O billing, memory limits, and Durable Objects coordination with a logical 4-module progression and balanced MC/short-answer assessments.

candidate_course.title: SQLite & Cloudflare D1 Internals: From B-Tree Pages to Edge SQL
candidate_course.description: An advanced systems course covering SQLite's page-based storage engine, WAL checkpointing, index selection mechanics, and Cloudflare D1's Durable Object-backed execution and Time Travel recovery.
candidate_course.target_audience: Advanced systems and database engineers

modules.title: Page Layout, B-Trees, and Overflow Pages in SQLite
modules.learning_objective: Analyze how SQLite stores tables as B+trees (`ROWID` keyed) and indexes as B-trees across fixed-size 4KB pages.
modules.summary: Breaks down interior vs. leaf pages, cell pointers, varint encoding, overflow page chains for large blobs, and `WITHOUT ROWID` clustered tables.
sample_question_prompts: Why does a secondary index lookup on a standard SQLite table require two B-tree traversals, and how does a covering index eliminate the second?
Explain when `WITHOUT ROWID` improves lookup locality and when it degrades write performance.

modules.title: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), Snapshot Isolation, and Checkpointing
modules.learning_objective: Trace how SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent readers alongside a single writer using the `-wal` file and `-shm` wal-index.
modules.summary: Examines frame appending, commit markers, reader mark end-points (`mxFrame`), and PASSIVE vs. RESTART vs. TRUNCATE checkpoint starvation.
sample_question_prompts: How does a reader determine which page version to read when multiple uncommitted and committed frames for page P exist in the WAL?
What causes WAL file growth under continuous read load, and how does SQLite resolve checkpoint starvation?

modules.title: Query Planning, Composite Indexes, and `sqlite_stat1`
modules.learning_objective: Interpret `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` output and design composite indexes that avoid temporary B-tree sorts.
modules.summary: Covers leftmost prefix rules, skip-scan optimizations, equality vs. range predicates in composite indexes, and how `PRAGMA optimize` updates cardinality histograms.
sample_question_prompts: Given `SELECT * FROM events WHERE org_id = ? AND created_at > ? ORDER BY created_at DESC`, design the optimal index and explain why `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` disappears.
What happens when an inequality column precedes an equality column in a composite index?

modules.title: Cloudflare D1 Architecture, Batching, and Time Travel
modules.learning_objective: Optimize Worker-to-D1 latency using `db.batch()` and explain how D1 provides point-in-time recovery and read scaling.
modules.summary: Explores how D1 runs atop Durable Objects storage, why pipelined `db.batch()` executes inside an implicit transaction, and how bookmark-based session consistency works across read replicas.
sample_question_prompts: Why does executing 20 sequential `await db.prepare().run()` calls from a Worker in Frankfurt against a D1 primary in US-East incur massive latency compared to `db.batch()`?
How do D1 Sessions API bookmarks ensure causal read-your-own-writes consistency across distributed read replicas?

expected.rationale: Rigorous, accurate coverage of SQLite internals (B+trees, WAL index, query planner) progressing naturally into Cloudflare D1's specific execution, batching, and replication semantics.

candidate_course.title: Replicated State Machines with Raft: Safety, Liveness, and Linearizability
candidate_course.description: A formal and practical examination of the Raft consensus protocol, focusing on the five safety invariants, subtle bugs in uncommitted log overwriting, and linearizable read optimizations.
candidate_course.target_audience: Advanced distributed systems engineers

modules.title: Terms, Logical Clocks, and Leader Election Safety
modules.learning_objective: Prove why at most one leader can be elected in a given term and how the Election Restriction prevents stale candidates from winning.
modules.summary: Analyzes Follower/Candidate/Leader state transitions, randomized election timeouts for liveness, and the two-tuple `(lastLogTerm, lastLogIndex)` log up-to-dateness comparison in `RequestVote`.
sample_question_prompts: Candidate A has last log entry `(term=4, index=10)` and Candidate B has `(term=5, index=8)`. Which log is more up-to-date according to Raft's `RequestVote` rules, and why?
How do randomized election timeouts solve split-vote livelock without sacrificing safety?

modules.title: Log Replication and the Log Matching Property
modules.learning_objective: Explain how `prevLogIndex` and `prevLogTerm` checks in `AppendEntries` inductively maintain the Log Matching Property.
modules.summary: Covers how leaders probe backward (`nextIndex`) to find where a follower's log diverges, truncate conflicting uncommitted suffix entries, and track `matchIndex`.
sample_question_prompts: Why is `nextIndex` initialized optimistically to `lastLogIndex + 1` while `matchIndex` is initialized conservatively to `0` upon leader election?
Show how `AppendEntries` consistency checks guarantee that if two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, their prefixes are identical.

modules.title: Commit Rules from Previous Terms (The Figure 8 Scenario)
modules.learning_objective: Explain why a Raft leader must never directly commit log entries from an earlier term by counting replicas alone.
modules.summary: Walks through Ongaro & Ousterhout's Figure 8 counterexample where an entry from an old term replicated on a majority can still be overwritten unless a current-term entry is committed first.
sample_question_prompts: Why does committing a no-op entry at the start of a new leader's term resolve the Figure 8 safety hazard and allow the leader to know the true `commitIndex`?
Trace the exact sequence of crashes in Figure 8 that allows a majority-replicated entry from Term 2 to be overwritten by a leader in Term 3.

modules.title: Linearizable Reads, ReadIndex, and LeaseRead Hazards
modules.learning_objective: Design linearizable read paths without writing to the Raft log using `ReadIndex` heartbeats.
modules.summary: Explains how a deposed leader partitioned from the cluster could serve stale reads, and how confirming leadership with a quorum heartbeat after recording `readIndex = commitIndex` preserves linearizability.
sample_question_prompts: Why is serving a read directly from the local state machine of a node that believes it is leader unsafe under network partitions?
Outline the exact steps of the `ReadIndex` protocol and explain why clock skew cannot violate its linearizability guarantees.

expected.rationale: Exceptional depth for an advanced learner, covering exact Raft safety invariants, the classic Figure 8 commit rule subtlety, and ReadIndex linearizability with both MC and short-answer questions.

user_context.prompt: I am a molecular biology graduate student starting a rotation in a genome editing lab. Teach me how to design sgRNAs for SpCas9 knockouts vs. cytosine/adenine base editors (CBE/ABE), including PAM constraints, activity windows, and bystander edit mitigation.
user_context.what_user_wants_to_learn: Practical guide RNA design rules for SpCas9 DSB knockouts versus CBE and ABE base editors, focusing on PAM positioning, deamination editing windows, and avoiding bystander mutations.

candidate_course.title: Precision Guide Design: From SpCas9 Knockouts to Cytosine & Adenine Base Editing
candidate_course.description: An applied wet-lab and computational design course covering RNP cleavage mechanics, PAM-relative activity windows for CBE/ABE architectures, and strategies to eliminate deleterious bystander edits.
candidate_course.target_audience: Intermediate molecular biologists and rotation students designing mammalian genome editing experiments

modules.title: SpCas9 Target Selection, PAM Recognition, and Frameshift Knockout Strategy
modules.learning_objective: Select optimal exons and 5'-NGG-3' PAM sites to induce nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) while minimizing off-target cleavage using CFD and MIT specificity scores.
modules.summary: Covers R-loop formation, HNH and RuvC nuclease cleavage 3 bp upstream of the NGG PAM, targeting early constitutive exons while avoiding the final exon or last 50–55 nt of the penultimate exon so premature stop codons trigger NMD.
sample_question_prompts: Why can targeting the last exon of a multi-exon gene with SpCas9 fail to produce a functional loss-of-function knockout even when a frameshift indel is confirmed by Sanger sequencing?
Given a target sequence 5'-ATGCGATCGATCGATCGATCGGG-3', identify the PAM and exact phosphodiester bond position cleaved by wild-type SpCas9.

modules.title: Cytosine and Adenine Base Editor Architectures (BE4max & ABE8e)
modules.learning_objective: Distinguish the deamination chemistry, Cas9 nickase (D10A) role, and uracil glycosylase inhibition in CBEs (C•G to T•A) versus evolved TadA deaminases in ABEs (A•T to G•C).
modules.summary: Explains why fusion of APOBEC/TadA to nCas9(D10A) exposes a single-stranded DNA R-loop bubble on the non-target strand, how UGI prevents base excision repair from reverting U:G intermediates, and how nicking the unedited target strand biases mismatch repair.
sample_question_prompts: What is the specific mechanistic role of the D10A nickase mutation and Uracil Glycosylase Inhibitor (UGI) in BE4max?
Which base transition can be directly catalyzed by an Adenine Base Editor (ABE8e) when targeting the coding or template strand?

modules.title: Editing Windows, PAM-Flexible Variants, and Bystander Edit Mitigation
modules.learning_objective: Place target nucleotides within canonical editing windows (positions 4–8 for SpCas9 CBE/ABE, counting PAM as 21–23) and select narrow-window or PAM-relaxed variants (SpG, SpRY, YE1) to avoid nonsynonymous bystander edits.
modules.summary: Walks through protospacer numbering (1 at 5' end, 20 adjacent to PAM), evaluating bystander C or A bases inside positions 4–8, checking if bystander edits are synonymous (wobble positions), or shifting the window using SpCas9-NG / SpG PAM variants.
sample_question_prompts: You want to install a disease-correcting A-to-G edit at protospacer position 6 using ABE8e, but there is another adenine at position 5. Under what codon condition is this bystander edit acceptable without changing deaminase variants?
How would switching from wild-type SpCas9-BE4 to YE1-BE4 or an SpG-PAM variant resolve a deleterious nonsynonymous bystander cytosine at position 8?

modules.title: Validation Assays and Off-Target Profiling (Cas-dependent vs. Cas-independent)
modules.learning_objective: Design amplicon deep sequencing (CRISPResso2) workflows and distinguish guide-dependent off-targets from guide-independent ssDNA/RNA deamination.
modules.summary: Compares Sanger trace deconvolution (EditR/TIDE) with NGS amplicon quantification using CRISPResso2, and contrasts Cas9-dependent off-target binding with stochastic TadA/APOBEC deamination in transcription bubbles.
sample_question_prompts: Why is whole-genome sequencing alone insufficient to efficiently detect Cas-independent transcriptomic off-target deamination by hyperactive CBEs?
In a CRISPResso2 output for a CBE experiment, you observe a 4% rate of C-to-G transversions and small indels at the target cytosine. What repair pathway caused this byproduct?

expected.rationale: The course directly addresses every part of the graduate student's prompt: SpCas9 knockout design (including NMD exon selection rules), CBE/ABE biochemical mechanisms (nCas9 D10A, UGI, TadA), exact protospacer numbering and activity windows (positions 4–8), and practical bystander mitigation strategies. Every module pairs multiple-choice and short-answer prompts at an appropriate intermediate molecular biology level.

How can high ambient hemoglobin mRNA in bone marrow samples create false marker gene signatures in non-erythroid clusters?

modules.title: UMI Count Modeling, Shifted Log Normalization, and Feature Selection
modules.learning_objective: Compare shifted logarithm normalization with Pearson residuals / Negative Binomial models, and select highly variable genes (HVGs) in a batch-aware manner.
modules.summary: Covers why zero-inflation in droplet UMI data is primarily driven by Poisson/Negative Binomial sampling dropout rather than structural biological zeros, and why `batch_key` must be specified during HVG selection.

modules.summary: Demonstrates how treating 10,000 cells from 6 donors as N=10,000 independent observations in a Wilcoxon rank-sum test conflates within-donor variance with between-donor variance, and also addresses double-dipping when testing marker genes between clusters defined by the same genes.

question.reference_answer: In TLS 1.3, the server's long-term X.509 private key is used exclusively to sign the handshake transcript (`CertificateVerify`) to prove identity and prevent active man-in-the-middle attacks; it is never used to encrypt or transport a pre-master secret.
